title: Attention kernel stability convergence and graceful fallback strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: After beginning rollout of FlashAttention v3 on our prefill path, we observed intermittent kernel selection oscillation under mixed sequence-length workloads. Oscillation produces bursts of increased p95/p99 latency and occasional OOMs on smaller-capacity workers. This ticket defines a strategy to stabilize kernel choice convergence, add guardrails and graceful fallback behavior, and create detection+rollback automation for regressions.

Background: The kernel selector takes runtime fingerprints (matrix shapes, sequence length histogram, quantization flags) and scores candidates. With v3 we introduced new variants that are higher throughput in steady-state but sensitive to cold KV-cache and microbatch variability. In practice, when request distributions change quickly (from short to long sequences) the selector can flip between v2/v3 candidates leading to thrashing during startup/warmup.

Goals:
- Reduce kernel selection oscillation events by 80% on mixed workloads in canary region.
- Ensure p99 latency regression is <5% compared to v2 baseline for 95% of traffic.
- Implement a graceful fallback path that avoids OOMs and keeps latency bounded when kernel choice is unstable.
- Add detection alerts and an automated rollback canary for the next runtime rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Canary (us-west-2) runs with v3 candidates for 72h and shows <20 oscillation events per 100k requests
p99 latency delta vs v2 baseline <= 5% for canonical short/long/mixed workloads
No OOM incidents attributable to kernel selection during canary (SLO: 99.99% success rate)
Fallback path exercised in controlled chaos test and returns safe v2 kernel within 50ms
Datadog dashboard + alert configured for oscillation-rate and kernel-switch-rate with runbook
design_decisions: Introduce hysteresis window in kernel scorer: persist top choice for N microbatches unless score delta > threshold
Add startup warmup: prefer conservative v2 variant for first X requests for a given model-instance until KV hit-rate stabilizes
Implement lightweight memory-safety probe before selecting aggressive v3 kernels to avoid OOM on evicted workspaces
Expose kernel-scorer debug trace to trace-id in logs for post-mortem and perf dashboards
proposed_tasks: Implement hysteresis_state in kernel selector and unit tests
Add KV hit-rate sampler and early conservative-selection hook
Build memory-safety probe and soft-fail path that downgrades to v2 on risk
Create Datadog dashboard panels and SLI/SLO checks for oscillation and p99 latency
Automate canary rollback: if oscillation-rate > threshold for 30m, flip canary traffic back and create incident
comments: 2026-02-26 Maya Chen: Triage notes - observed two modes of oscillation: (1) warmup thrash when KV miss-rate falls, (2) steady-state flip during microbatch bursts. Recommend combined hysteresis + warmup approach.

2026-03-02 Rajesh Nair: Prototype hysteresis implemented; unit tests added. Initial microbench shows oscillation events reduced by ~60% on synthetic mixed workload (300k requests). Need integration test with real canary traffic.

2026-03-05 SRE (Leah Park): Ran chaos test with sequence-length spike; fallback path successfully downgraded 12 canary instances without OOMs. Observed p99 spike ~8% during transition; working on reducing probe latency.

2026-03-08 Maya Chen: Benchmarked v2 vs v3 candidate selection timeline. v3 throughput win appears after ~250 tokens produced per request when KV-hit stabilizes. Added conservative window to prefer v2 for first 3 requests per model-instance.

2026-03-11 Rajesh Nair: Deployed PRs to canary (us-west-2). Preliminary Datadog snapshot: oscillation events down 78% vs previous canary; p99 delta +3.6% on mixed workload. Proceeding to extended 72h canary and will enable automated rollback thresholds post-72h if stable.
